Synthetic Methods
Copper-Catalyzed Synthesis of Tetrasubstituted Allenes from
Quaternary Ammonium Salts and Grignard Reagents
Shengming Ma,*[a, b] Qi Liu,[a] Xinjun Tang,[a] and Yujuan Cai[a]
Abstract: Although the synthesis of allenes has made con-
siderable progress, methods for tetrasubstituted allenes
are still limited. In this paper,t he CuBr2-catalyzed cross-
coupling reaction of Grignardr eagents and propargylic
ammonium salts in tetrahydrofuran at 60 8Cu nder argon
delivered tetrasubstituted allenes in good to excellent
yields. The reactioni st hought to proceed by an SN2’ path-
way.
Allenes are important units of naturalp roducts andb iologically
active compounds.[1–2] Moreover,t hey are also useful building
blocks in organic synthesis as demonstrated over the last few
decades.[3–17] Therefore, exploring simple and useful methods
to synthesize varioust ypeso fa llenes is of great importance.[18]
Especially,m ethods for the synthesis of tetrasubstituted allenes
are still limited (Scheme 1).[19] In 2010, Zhang et al. developed
ap alladium-catalyzed three-component tandemM ichael addi-
tion/cross-coupling reactiono fe nyne ketones with alcohols as
nucleophiles and aryl halidest os ynthesize tetrasubstituted al-
lenyl ketones.[19i] Davies et al. reported the reaction of propar-
gylic alcohols with methyl diazoacetates to produce tetrasub-
stituteda llenest hrough [2,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement.[19j]
Sawamura’s group reported ac opper-catalyzed coupling be-
tween propargylic phosphates and alkyl-9-BBN to synthesize
tri- and tetrasubstituted allenes (BBN = borabicyclo[3.3.1]nona-
ne).[19k] In 2015, our group disclosed aC @Hb ond activation-
based method to form tetrasubstituted optically active allenes,
in which the C@Ct riple bonds of 2-alkynylic carbonates were
regiospecifically inserted by an aryl–[Rh] through concerted
metalation/deprotonation (CMD)f ollowed by b-elimination.[19p]
More recently,L ist et al. reported ac hiral disulfonimidec ata-
lyzed alkynylogousM ukaiyama aldol reaction to synthesize
chiral tetrasubstituted allenoates.[19x]
Considering our previous report on KA2 reactions (three-
component coupling reaction of ketone–amine–alkyne to pro-
duce secondary propargylamines) for the efficient synthesis of
propargylic amines,[20] we attempted to apply the reactiono f
propargylic amines and Grignardr eagents to generate tetra-
substituted allenes. However,t he reactionf ailed to yield the
desired product [Eq. (1)].
Thus, we envisioned that if we could transform such type of
propargylic amines into ammoniums alts, the pyrrolidinium
part would be ab etter leaving group to form allenes
(Scheme 2). To the best of our knowledge, using propargylic
ammonium salts as the precursors of allenes hasn ot been well
established, and most of those transformations werea chieved
by reactingw ith LiAlH4.[21] Onlyf ew reactionso fp ropargylic
ammonium salts with Grignard reagents or organocopper re-
agents have been reported.[22] And there are some limitations,
such as narrow substrates copes and forming alkyne as side
products.
We startedo ur investigation with quaternary ammonium
salt 1a ,w hich was prepared through methylation with iodo-
methane in acetonitrile at room temperature.I nt he absence
of any copper catalyst, the desired product 2a was formed in
73 %y ield when 1.8 equivalents of ethyl magnesium bromide
were added (Table 1, entry 1). After screening, it was observed
that the optimal loading of ethyl magnesium bromide was
1.6 equivalents (entries 1–3). When 10 mol %o fC uI was added,
2a was afforded in 86 %y ield (entry 4).
The reaction of ammonium salt 1b with ethyl magnesium
bromide under the same conditions would generate the unde-
sired trisubstituted allene product 3b in 6% yield as the by-
product (Table 2, entry 1). The employment of 10 mol %C uBr2
insteado fC uI led to ab etter selectivity (entry 2), and to our
delight, 2b was obtained in ah ighery ield of 90 %. Increasing
the amount of CuBr2 could effectively reduce the formation of
undesired trisubstituted allenes 3b (entries 3–5). When using
20 mol %o fC uBr2,u ndesired product 3b was not formed at

(20 mol %) in tetrahydrofuran at 60 8Cu nder argon atmos-
phere.
With the optimized conditions in hand, we investigated the
substrate scope of the reaction. At first, different propargylic
ammonium salts were tested with ethyl magnesium bromide:
R3 could be alkyl groups (Table 3, entries 1a nd 2). With R1
being an aryl group, the substrates with electron-withdrawing
groups (entries 3–5) gave slightly lower yields than those with
electron-donating methoxy group (entry 6). With R2,R 3 being
-(CH2)5-, tetrasubstituted allene 2g wasp roduced in 81 %y ield
(entry 7). Allene 2h with four alkyl substituents could also be
synthesized through this methodi n8 8% yield (entry 8).

Various Grignardr eagents were applicable for the method.
In addition to ethyl magnesium bromide, methyl magnesium
bromide and pentyl magnesium bromide also worked to
afford the relatedp roducts in 84 %a nd 90 %y ield, respectively
(Table 4, entries 1a nd 2). Using freshly prepared phenyl mag-
nesium bromide, ammonium salt 1h was converted to tetra-
substituted allene 2k in 90 %y ield (entry 3). Gratifyingly, p-
chlorophenyl magnesium bromide alsow orked( entry 4). On
the other hand, aryl Grignardr eagents with the electron-do-
nating methoxy group underwent coupling reactions with am-
monium salt 1h successfully to afford corresponding allenes in
80–85 yields (entries 5a nd 6). Benzylm agnesium chloride and
allyl magnesium bromide were also suitablef or this reaction
(entries 7a nd 8).
In the absence of copper catalysis, ammonium salt 1i could
also react with phenylm agnesium bromide to afford 2q in
85 %y ield [Eq. (2)].I sobutyl magnesium bromide was also ap-
plicable with the catalysis of 10 mol %C uI [Eq. (3)].A dditional-
ly,i ti sc onvenient to conductt he reaction on ag ram scale to
afford 2b in 94 %y ield [Eq. (4)].
According to the previous reports,[19k, u] it is believed that
ac atalytic cycle starts with the transmetalation of Grignardr e-
agents to form organocopper(II) species A. A proceeds an SN2’-
type reactionw ith ammonium salts 1 to generate allenes 2
(Scheme 3).
In summary,t he reaction of readilya vailable quaternary am-
monium salts andG rignard reagents to produce tetrasubstitut-
ed allenesu nder CuBr2 catalysis proceeded smoothly under
mild conditions in good to excellent yields. An SN2’ mechanism
was proposed. Further study on asymmetric version is ongoing
in our group.

Procedure for gram-scale synthesis of 2b :T oa dried Schlenk
tube were added CuBr2 (0.3108 g, 1.4 mmol), 1b (2.7825 g,
7m mol), and tetrahydrofuran (35 mL) sequentially under argon at-

was added dropwise with stirring. The Schlenk tube was then
